These lessons can help develop motor skills, imagination and creative thinking. Mom can help their child or watch and take pictures. Have fun with family and friends without strangers. quotes.author: Anna Asgaraly
quotes.text: Had the loveliest experience here, loved how our pieces turned out! Asli was so knowledgeable, patient and kind with us. Will definitely be coming back!

quotes.author: Ellen
quotes.text: This was such a great place to start pottery!! Alvina was a perfect teacher and amazing to talk to. We went for the pottery date and had the best time excited to go again!

quotes.author: Horlane Mbayo
quotes.text: Laura was the best teacher and so kind. We made an adorable bowl. I want 4 of them now. Can’t wait to see it after it’s glazed. Thank you Laura for such a fun afternoon.

quotes.author: Gabby Whitehead
quotes.text: Amazing pottery class experience with Laura and Kelly. Great teachers and so sweet. Our group ended up with so many cute bowls and mugs that we can’t wait to use.

quotes.author: Alyssa Osani
quotes.text: I had so much fun! I went into this prepared to completely make a lump, but Laura and Kelly were so informative and supportive! I highly recommend and can't wait to try making pottery again! ❤️

quotes.author: Malvika Gupta
quotes.text: It was a first time we tried pottery and had an amazing experience. Kelly was our teacher and she was very patient and informative. We had an amazing time and it felt very therapeutic!! We will come back!!

quotes.author: Leanne Coupland
quotes.text: Me and my friends had the best afternoon at Pottery Studio! Aya our instructor was so lovely and super helpful! Such a cute way to spend time with friends!

quotes.author: Chloe Ramirez
quotes.text: As a studio instructor at Pottery Studio 1, I’ve seen how pottery helps kids develop focus, patience, and creativity. It’s also a wonderful bonding activity for parents and children — creating something with your hands brings everyone closer together.
When I need to make something I’m often mesmerized or haunted by an idea or by a piece of poetry… I am grounded in history, the history and culture of the materials I use.

There is collaboration between the clay and myself — the clay tells me what direction to take.’ My pots are traditional, and I follow the techniques of my ancestors — except for the asymmetricals I have created.
